results.name: Performance-Weighted Analyst Estimates
results.description: This dataset applies an enhanced version of the StarMine SmartEstimate model to a broad universe of stocks and financial metrics, leveraging analyst estimate data from IBES. It calculates a performance score for each analyst based on their historical forecasting accuracy and incorporates the recency of their estimates. By combining these two factors, the model generates "smart estimates" that are more predictive than simple consensus means. The dataset includes modules for analyst innovation, outlier handling, and time-series feature generation, making it a robust tool for identifying which analyst forecasts are likely to be most accurate. This can help investors and researchers anticipate earnings surprises and price movements, as changes in smart estimates often precede market reactions.

response_sample.name: Hello Quants!
response_sample.task: Try entering the code -returns in the left screen and press the Simulate button. Once you've run the simulation, make sure to click the RESULTS checkbox to view your backtest results. Don't forget to check your performance!
response_sample.hint: Enter -returns and run the simulation.

response_sample.name: What is an Alpha?
response_sample.task: Try simulating an Alpha by applying rank() to -returns.
response_sample.hint: Enter rank(-returns) and run the simulation.

response_sample.name: What is an Alpha? (2)
response_sample.task: Simulate any Alpha you want and check the results.
response_sample.hint: Click on the 'Example' button in the bottom left corner for an example Alpha. Simulate and check the results.

response_sample.name: What's going on in the platform?
response_sample.task: Change Neutralization to None in Settings and check the results.
response_sample.hint: Set Neutralization to None in Settings and simulate the alpha.

response_sample.name: What's going on in the platform? (2)
response_sample.task: In Settings, set Neutralization to Market and apply a value of 3 or higher for Decay, then simulate the Alpha.
response_sample.hint: Set Neutralization to Market and Decay to 3 or higher in Settings.

response_sample.name: Settings
response_sample.task: Simulate any Alpha you want and check the results.
response_sample.hint: Click on the 'Example' button in the bottom left corner for an example Alpha. Simulate and check the results.

response_sample.name: Finding data fields
response_sample.task: Try simulating an Alpha using data fields other than returns.
response_sample.hint:
You can explore data fields by clicking Data at the top of the screen.
The simulator also provides auto-completion when you start typing the data field.

response_sample.name: Finding Operators
response_sample.task: Try simulating an Alpha using a Time Series operator.
response_sample.hint:
Click Learn at the top of the screen and go to Operator to see available operators.
They are categorized by type, and Time Series operators are grouped together.
Most time series operators start with ts_.

response_sample.name: About Price Volume Alpha
response_sample.task: Try simulating an Alpha that includes vwap/close and has a turnover below 70%.
response_sample.hint:
Simulate an alpha that includes vwap/close.
You can control alpha's turnover through various methods like Decay, trade_when, etc.

response_sample.name: About Close Location Value
response_sample.task: Create an Alpha with a Sharpe ratio above 1.4 using all four data fields: high, low, close, volume.
response_sample.hint:
The CLV expression has a range of -1 to 1.
Write an alpha that allocates more positions to stocks with higher volume.

response_sample.name: About Momentum Effect
response_sample.task: Try using the count of days with price increases over a year in your Alpha.
response_sample.hint: Follow the instructions step by step to create positive days.

response_sample.name: About Logical Operators
response_sample.task: Try creating an Alpha using trade_when and positive_days.
response_sample.hint: Positive days work better with conditions. Try adding a volume-related condition.

response_sample.name: About Alpha Submit Criteria
response_sample.task: Try creating a submittable Alpha!
response_sample.hint: Review everything you've learned so far and create a submittable alpha.
response_sample.answer: We encourage you to work through this problem on your own!

response_sample.name: About Fundamental Data
response_sample.task: Assets, equity, and debtare basic fundamental data fields from the balance sheet. Come up with alpha ideas related to these three data fields, and simulate an alpha that includes at least one of these data fields.
response_sample.hint: Simulate an alpha using one or more data fields among assets, equity, and debt.

response_sample.name: About Combining PV and Fundamental Data
response_sample.task: Create an Alpha using operating_income and market capitalization (cap) with your preferred comparison method.
response_sample.hint: Divide operating_income by cap.

response_sample.name: About Combining PV and Fundamental Data (2)
response_sample.task: Create an Alpha using EBITDA and Enterprise Value.
response_sample.hint: Simulate an alpha using ebitda and enterprise_value.

response_sample.name: About TS & CS Operators
response_sample.task: Create and simulate an Alpha comparing OEY using ts_rank().
response_sample.hint: Apply ts_rank() to OEY.

response_sample.name: About Universe
response_sample.task: Simulate an Alpha in various universes such as TOP1000, TOP500, TOP200.
response_sample.hint: Apply ts_rank() to OEY and simulate in a universe other than TOP3000.

response_sample.name: Summary: Fundamental Alpha
response_sample.task:
Try creating a submittable Alpha!
Also check if the same formula is working well in other delay settings or universes
response_sample.hint: Review everything you've learned so far and create a submittable alpha.
response_sample.answer: Try solving this problem on your own!

response_sample.name: About Option Alpha
response_sample.task: Try creating an Alpha using implied volatility (implied_volatility_~).
response_sample.hint: You can access data fields by appending option type and maturity, such as implied_volatility_call_120, implied_volatility_put_180.

response_sample.name: About Option Alpha (2)
response_sample.task: Create an Alpha comparing call option implied volatility (implied_volatility_call_{expiry}) and put option implied volatility (implied_volatility_put_{expiry}).
response_sample.hint: Comparing options with the same maturity, like implied_volatility_call_120 - implied_volatility_put_120, provides more accurate comparisons.

response_sample.name: About Neutralization
response_sample.task: Create an Alpha incorporating all of these elements!
response_sample.hint: Try creating groups using rank(historical_volatility_120) with bucket().

response_sample.hint: Review everything you've learned so far and create a submittable alpha.

response_sample.name: About Sentiment Alpha
response_sample.task: Try simulating an Alpha comparing the two data fields scl12_buzz and volume using ts_regression.
response_sample.hint: To understand the relative size of scl12_buzz compared to volume, in ts_regression(y,x,lookback_days), scl12_buzz should be y and volume should be x.

response_sample.name: About News Alpha
response_sample.task:
Use vec_avg(nws12_afterhsz_sl) to calculate the average sentiment from news data for each company.
Use ts_sum or ts_mean (ts operator) and rank to set proper condition.
Use if_else or form of ?: to implement the Alpha idea.
response_sample.hint:
Rank the sum of news sentiment (nws12_afterhsz_sl) over time.
- High ranked stocks ? +1 (momentum)
- Low ranked stocks ? short position based on recent returns (reversion)
